tools.refinance-calculator.metadata.desc: Compare your current loan with a refinance option and calculate the break-even point and total savings.
tools.refinance-calculator.faqs.0.questi: How do I know if refinancing my mortgage is worth it?
tools.refinance-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Refinancing is generally worth considering when you can lower your interest rate by at least 0.5–1%, plan to stay in the home long enough to pass the break-even point, or need to switch from an adjustable-rate to a fixed-rate mortgage. Use the break-even calculation to see how many months of savings it takes to recoup closing costs.
tools.refinance-calculator.faqs.1.questi: What is the break-even point on a mortgage refinance?
tools.refinance-calculator.faqs.1.answer: The break-even point is the number of months it takes for your monthly payment savings to equal the total closing costs of the refinance. For example, if closing costs are $4,500 and you save $150/month, your break-even point is 30 months. If you plan to stay in the home beyond this point, refinancing saves you money.
tools.refinance-calculator.faqs.2.questi: What are typical closing costs for a mortgage refinance?
tools.refinance-calculator.faqs.2.answer: Typical refinance closing costs range from 2% to 5% of the loan amount and may include application fees, appraisal fees, title insurance, origination fees, and prepaid items like taxes and insurance escrow. On a $280,000 loan, expect $5,600 to $14,000 in closing costs.
tools.refinance-calculator.faqs.3.questi: What are mortgage points and should I buy them?
tools.refinance-calculator.faqs.3.answer: Mortgage discount points are upfront fees paid to the lender to reduce your interest rate, typically costing 1% of the loan amount per point and reducing the rate by about 0.25%. Buying points makes sense if you plan to keep the loan long enough for the monthly savings to exceed the upfront cost.
tools.refinance-calculator.faqs.4.questi: Does refinancing restart my mortgage clock?
tools.refinance-calculator.faqs.4.answer: Yes. Refinancing replaces your existing loan with a new one, so if you refinance into a new 30-year term after paying 5 years on your original mortgage, you will have 30 new years of payments. However, you can choose a shorter term (such as 15 or 20 years) to avoid extending your payoff date significantly.
tools.refinance-calculator.faqs.5.questi: Can I refinance with bad credit?
tools.refinance-calculator.faqs.5.answer: While it is harder to refinance with a low credit score, options exist. FHA streamline refinances, VA IRRRLs, and USDA streamline refinances have more lenient credit requirements. Conventional refinances typically require a minimum score of 620, though better rates are available at 740 and above.

tools.sleep-calculator.metadata.descript: Calculate ideal bedtimes and wake times based on 90-minute sleep cycles.
tools.sleep-calculator.faqs.0.question: What is a sleep cycle?
tools.sleep-calculator.faqs.0.answer: A sleep cycle lasts about 90 minutes and moves through light, deep, and REM sleep. Waking between cycles (rather than during deep sleep) helps you feel more refreshed. Most adults need 5-6 complete cycles (7.5-9 hours).
tools.sleep-calculator.faqs.1.question: Why do I feel groggy after 8 hours of sleep?
tools.sleep-calculator.faqs.1.answer: You may be waking during deep sleep. Try adjusting your alarm by 15-30 minutes. Aim for complete 90-minute cycles, so 7.5 hours (5 cycles) may feel better than 8 hours.
tools.sleep-calculator.faqs.2.question: How long does it take to fall asleep?
tools.sleep-calculator.faqs.2.answer: The average person takes about 10-20 minutes to fall asleep. This calculator uses 15 minutes. Adjust your bedtime accordingly if you fall asleep faster or slower.

tools.square-root-calculator.faqs.0.ques: How do I calculate a square root?
tools.square-root-calculator.faqs.0.answ: The square root of a number x is the value that, when multiplied by itself, equals x. For example, √144 = 12 because 12 × 12 = 144. This calculator handles any positive number and simplifies radicals.
tools.square-root-calculator.faqs.1.answ: A perfect square is a number whose square root is an integer. Examples: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100, 121, 144, 169, 196, 225.
tools.square-root-calculator.faqs.2.answ: Factor out perfect squares from under the radical. For example, √72 = √(36 × 2) = 6√2. Find the largest perfect square factor and move its root outside.

tools.standard-deviation-calculator.meta: Calculate the standard deviation and variance for sample or population data sets.
tools.standard-deviation-calculator.faqs: Standard deviation measures how spread out data is from the mean. A low standard deviation means data points cluster close to the mean. A high standard deviation means they are widely spread. It is expressed in the same units as the data.

Population standard deviation (σ) divides by N — used when you have all data points. Sample standard deviation (s) divides by N-1 — used when you have a sample from a larger population. The N-1 correction (Bessel's correction) makes the sample standard deviation an unbiased estimator.

A z-score tells you how many standard deviations a value is from the mean. Z=0 is at the mean. Z=1 is 1 standard deviation above. Z=-2 is 2 below. About 68% of data falls within ±1 standard deviation and 95% within ±2.

tools.typing-speed-test.metadata.title: Typing Speed Test
tools.typing-speed-test.metadata.descrip: Test your typing speed with WPM, CPM, and accuracy. 60-second countdown with sample text.
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.0.question: What is a good typing speed?
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.0.answer: A good typing speed for casual typists is about 40-50 WPM. Professional typists typically reach 65-75 WPM, and expert typists can exceed 100 WPM. For most office jobs, 50-60 WPM is considered proficient.
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.1.question: How is WPM calculated?
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.1.answer: WPM (words per minute) is calculated by dividing the total characters typed by 5 (the standard word length), then dividing by the elapsed time in minutes. Net WPM subtracts errors, while gross/raw WPM counts all keystrokes.
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.2.question: What is the average typing speed?
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.2.answer: The average typing speed is about 40 WPM for casual computer users. Students and professionals who type regularly average around 50-60 WPM. Practiced touch typists typically reach 60-80 WPM.
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.3.question: How can I type faster?
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.3.answer: To improve your typing speed: learn touch typing (using all fingers without looking at the keyboard), practice at least 15 minutes daily, focus on accuracy before speed, maintain proper posture, and take regular typing tests to track progress.
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.4.question: What is the difference between gross WPM and net WPM?
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.4.answer: Gross (raw) WPM counts all your keystrokes divided by 5, regardless of accuracy. Net WPM only counts correctly typed characters divided by 5. Net WPM more accurately reflects your effective typing speed.
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.5.question: Is 40 WPM good?
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.5.answer: 40 WPM is about average for casual typists and sufficient for most general computer use. However, for professional roles involving heavy typing, you will benefit from improving to 50-60+ WPM. With practice, most people can reach this level.
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.6.question: What is the fastest recorded typing speed?
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.6.answer: The fastest recorded typing speed is 216 WPM, achieved by Stella Pajunas on an IBM electric typewriter in 1946. In modern times, competitive typists on platforms like TypeRacer and Monkeytype often exceed 150-200 WPM over short bursts.
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.7.question: How accurate should I be when typing?
tools.typing-speed-test.faqs.7.answer: You should aim for at least 95% accuracy, with 97-99% being ideal. High accuracy matters more than raw speed because errors slow you down through corrections. Focus on accuracy first; speed will improve naturally with practice.

tools.walking-calorie-calculator.metadat: Estimate calories burned walking based on weight, distance or steps, and speed.
How many calories do you burn walking a mile?

As a general estimate, a 150-170 lb person walking 1 mile at a moderate pace (3 mph) burns about 80-100 calories. However, the exact number depends on your weight, speed, and terrain. Heavier people burn more calories per mile, and walking uphill significantly increases calorie burn. Use this calculator to enter your specific details for a personalized estimate.
How does walking speed affect calories burned?

Walking faster burns more calories per minute because it requires more energy. A brisk 3.5 mph walk has a MET value of about 4.3, while a slow 2 mph stroll has a MET of 2.8 — meaning brisk walking burns about 50% more calories per minute. A power walk at 4.5 mph can burn more than double the calories of a slow stroll in the same time.
Does walking uphill burn more calories?

Yes, walking uphill significantly increases calorie burn. Walking uphill at a 5% incline burns 30-40% more calories than walking at the same speed on flat ground. A steep 10-15% incline can nearly double the calorie burn. This calculator adjusts the MET value based on the incline you select.
Is the MET formula for walking calories accurate?

The MET (Metabolic Equivalent of Task) formula — calories = MET x weight (kg) x time (hours) — is the standard method used by exercise physiologists and is fairly accurate for most people. Individual variation of 10-20% is normal due to differences in fitness level, walking economy, and body composition. It provides a reliable estimate for tracking and planning purposes.
How many steps are in a mile?

The average person takes about 2,000 steps per mile at a moderate walking pace. This varies with stride length, which depends on height, leg length, and walking speed. At a slow pace you might take 2,400 steps per mile, while a power walk might only require 1,800. This calculator estimates steps based on your walking speed.

tools.weight-loss-calculator.metadata.de: Estimate how long it takes to reach your target weight based on daily calorie deficit.
tools.weight-loss-calculator.faqs.0.ques: How does this weight loss calculator work?
tools.weight-loss-calculator.faqs.0.answ: This calculator uses the Mifflin-St Jeor formula to estimate your basal metabolic rate (BMR), then multiplies by an activity factor to get your total daily energy expenditure (TDEE). It then subtracts daily calorie deficits of 250, 500, 750, and 1,000 calories to show how quickly you will reach your target weight at each pace. One pound of body fat equals about 3,500 calories, so a 500-calorie daily deficit leads to about 1 pound of loss per week.
